item.title: Former Man Utd star Ander Herrera hails Boca Juniors as 'the biggest fan movement in the world' and names Superclasico as 'the best football atmosphere' of his career
item.description: Boca Juniors v Barcelona SC - Copa CONMEBOL Libertadores - Getty Images Sport Former Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Ander Herrera has reflected on his unforgettable spell in Argentine football by paying a glowing tribute to the devotion of Boca Juniors supporters. Now back in his homeland with boyhood club Real Zaragoza, the veteran Spaniard insists nothing in Europe matched life in Buenos Aires. Spanish veteran recalls Argentine spell Speaking during an appearance on Mario's Journey , the former Spain international explained that the bond between the Xeneize faithful and their famous shirt eclipsed everything else he witnessed across his decorated career. Having experienced intense European nights in England and France, the playmaker was still blown away by the daily emotion surrounding La Bombonera. Summing up the club's global reach, he declared that "Boca is the biggest fan movement in the world." Supporters treat club like religion Beyond matchdays, the midfielder was struck by how deeply the Buenos Aires heavyweights are woven into the everyday lives of local residents, who routinely gathered outside hotels and training facilities just to catch a glimpse of the squad. Detailing the emotional scenes he witnessed on team trips and around the training ground, Herrera said: "For Boca fans, Boca comes before their families. People were crying. They came to see us at the training ground when we left in the cars. Boca is madness. It's a religion. But that's why Boca is what it is. Boca is the biggest popular movement in the world. That's it." River Plate victory stands out When asked to pinpoint the pinnacle of his stint in South America, the Spaniard singled out a memorable 2-0 home triumph over fierce city rivals River Plate in the Superclasico. Describing the sensation of emerging from the tunnel into a bouncing cauldron at La Bombonera, Herrera added: "The best football atmosphere I've ever experienced was Boca-River, which we won 2-0. You go up the stairs and see 55,000 crazy people and it's something unique. It's the biggest club in South America. I wasn't born a Boca fan, but I'll be a Boca fan for the rest of my life." Boyhood club occupies final chapter Having fulfilled a lifelong ambition by sampling the intensity of Argentine football, Herrera is now focused on seeing out the closing stages of his playing days back in Spain with Zaragoza . While his on-pitch duties lie in his native country, the midfielder intends to follow results at La Bombonera closely from afar as a devoted supporter. His glowing endorsement further cements the Superclasico's reputation as one of sport's greatest spectacles.

item.title: Xavier, Mercy cross country teams used depth to set SCC records. Now they eye CIAC titles
item.description: Xavier has relied on strong pack running behind juniors (left to right) Quentin Koch, Holden Hines, James Perrault, Nolan O'Connor and Alex Brown. They are all seen here running during the 43rd Wickham Park XC Invitational cross country meet. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) Middletown's Xavier and Mercy high schools have been intertwined since the beginning. The schools were planned at the same time, with both conceived by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Norwich. Both opened in 1963, with Mercy students attending classes on the second floor of Xavier until a separate building was completed in 1965. The schools' cross country programs were also intertwined at the SCC championships on Oct. 21. Both teams set SCC meet records for the lowest winning score in their respective races. The Falcons needed just 24 points to win, besting their own mark of 28 set in 2006. The Tigers needed just 23 points to win, besting the 29 scored by Guilford in 2008. It was a tremendous performance by both teams. Just how dominant were Xavier and Mercy? Each team had five first-team All-SCC honorees. First-team status is earned by runners finishing in places 1-12 at the championship meet. Each team was paced by a junior individual champion: Xavier's Holden Hines (15:45.0) and Mercy's Cora Wasiolek (18:52.6). Xavier's top five (scoring) runners finished in the top 10. All juniors, they were Hines, Quentin Koch (2nd), James Perrault (4th), Nolan O'Connor (7th) and Alex Brown (10th). Mercy's top five runners finished in the top 11. They were junior Cora Wasiolek (1st), junior Alyson Low (4th), junior Ruby Kuselias (6th), senior Madalena D'Andrea (9th) and sophomore McKenna Ouellette (11th). For Xavier, the SCC championship was the program's 11th straight title and 20th overall. "The championship streak is something we're proud of, but continued success requires more than following a series of X's and O's," Falcons coach Chris Stonier said. "It's about continually improving ourselves and the people around us, both as runners and as people." "The whole team holds each other accountable and wants what's best for the person next to them," Xavier junior James Perrault said. For Mercy, the SCC championship was the program's third straight and fifth overall. "One of the great values of this year's team and some of our teams in the past is a commitment to being selfless," Tigers coach Matt Conyers said. "I think this year's group has executed on that philosophy as well as any group and we're seeing the results of it." Pack mentalities Xavier and Mercy both subscribe to pack running, as do plenty of other cross country programs. The Falcons and Tigers have both excelled in that department so far this year. item.description: Ryan O'Donoghue, Kobe McDonald and Darragh Beirne are three of Mayo's six All-Stars [Getty Images] Six of the team that helped Mayo end their 75-year wait for All-Ireland glory have been recognised in the 2026 All-Stars. Defenders Sam Callinan and Enda Hession and forwards Darragh Beirne and Kobe McDonald have been selected alongside Footballer of the Year nominees Jack Carney and Ryan O'Donoghue, who also won an All-Star in 2021. McDonald - who has since embarked on his Australian Football League career - and Beirne are also nominated for Young Footballer of the year. Kerry superstar David Clifford - who is also competing for his fourth Footballer of the Year title - picks up his seventh award alongside Kingdom team-mates Jason Foley and Shane Murphy. Clifford's seventh All-Star brings him alongside Kerry great Mikey Sheehy and closer to Colm Cooper (eight) and Pat Spillane (nine). There are eight different counties represented - the most since 2010 - and 11 first-time winners, the most since 2022. Enduring memories and 'imposter syndrome' - The GAA Social meets Mayo star Carney There are three first-time inclusions from Ulster counties: dynamic Armagh wing-back Jarly Og Burns, totemic Tyrone midfielder Conn Kilpatrick and skilful Monaghan wing-forward Stephen O'Hanlon. Burns - the son of GAA president Jarlath Burns - was instrumental in helping Armagh end an 18-year wait for an Ulster title, while Kilpatrick shone for the Red Hands before helping his club Edendork win their first Tyrone championship last week. Westmeath captain Ronan Wallace is recognised after helping the Lake County win their first Leinster SFC title in 22 years, while Louth's Dara McDonnell is included at centre-back after starring in the Wee County's run to the All-Ireland semi-finals. McDonnell is also up for Young Footballer of the Year against McDonald and Beirne. Niall Scully is Dublin's sole inclusion, his second All-Star after picking up his first in 2020. "An incredible football season that was crammed full of memorable twists and turns has a legacy in this All-Star football team, one that reflects just how competitive our game is now," said GAA president Burns. "Mayo have had their season rightly rewarded, and with eight counties represented and 11 first-time winners, there will be clubs all over Ireland that wake up and share in this fantastic news and feel that they have played a part in this success. "It will be an extraordinary honour and privilege to be able to present my own club's first-ever All-Star award to Jarly Óg and Silverbridge." item.title: Francesco Bagnaia calls Sepang his “best chance” and vows to “risk more”
item.description: Motorsport photo Francesco Bagnaia says he is willing to take more risks at this weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix, describing Sepang as his “best chance” to secure a strong result before leaving Ducati. The Italian has a strong track record at the Sepang International Circuit, having won two of the last four grands prix in Malaysia. Last year, Bagnaia put his GP24 on pole and won the sprint race, despite suffering the same problems that plagued much of his campaign. With the 2026 season nearing its conclusion, the three-time world champion sees Sepang as his best opportunity to rediscover some enjoyment on the GP26 after what has been a frustrating year. “I'm really looking forward to riding here. I love the track, and I think it's the best chance I have to enjoy it a little bit more,” he said on Thursday. “I will give my maximum. I will risk more to enjoy. “It will be very difficult, but also last year I was without anything on my bike and I did pole and then I won a sprint. Then I had an issue in the race. This year is more or less the same, but I would like to enjoy. “The test went well here. I was quite fast and also the pace was strong, so it would be good.” Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team The Sepang circuit was due to undergo extensive renovation work this year, but those plans were later scrapped. Only part of the track has been resurfaced since last year’s race, but Formula 1 drivers already reported that asphalt was breaking up during the Bahrain GP in Malaysia earlier this month. Michelin had brought an additional medium rear tyre that was originally designed for the resurfaced track, while riders also have a soft and a hard tyre at their disposal. “The tyres are different,” Bagnaia said. “They brought different tyres compared to the test, because they were thinking that the circuit was resurfacing, but they had some issue with shipping the material, so the asphalt is the same. “Apart from that Formula 1 scratched the straights. So let's see. It will be interesting. The new medium tyre may work and it will be interesting to try.” Read Also: Alex Marquez moves to end MotoGP Qatar GP speculation: 'The race is confirmed' Jorge Martin braced for “really difficult, painful” MotoGP weekend with broken arm To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde makes heartfelt gesture to help victims of tragic train accident
item.description: Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde makes heartfelt gesture to help victims of tragic train accident It was a dark day in Spain on Wednesday, with Real Madrid among the football clubs mourning the victims of the devastating train accident in Urda, Toledo. With dozens of people losing their lives and many others injured, the tragedy prompted an outpouring of solidarity across the country. The tragedy also prompted a meaningful gesture from Los Blancos captain Federico Valverde. The Uruguayan has gone beyond expressing condolences. Valverde has used his substantial social media following to help families searching for loved ones who remain missing following the accident. Valverde uses his platform to help families of missing passengers The Uruguayan midfielder shared an emotional message on Instagram, offering his support to those affected and expressing his willingness to assist in any possible way. “As captain of Real Madrid, I make myself available to help in whatever way is necessary and to assist in spreading information that could help locate missing people,” Valverde wrote. The 28-year-old subsequently shared several Instagram stories containing appeals from relatives desperately seeking information about missing family members. Federico Valverde shared several stories. (Source: Instagram) With more than 21 million followers on the platform, Valverde’s involvement helped bring these appeals to a considerably wider audience. He also circulated useful information about blood donation locations and emergency contact numbers. Real Madrid also pay tribute to the victims The club responded to the tragedy by issuing an official statement expressing condolences to the victims’ families and solidarity with those injured. Mourinho and his players also observed a minute’s silence before Wednesday’s training session, while Madrid cancelled a scheduled commercial event. Real Madrid should be proud of having Fede Valverde as their captain. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) Meanwhile, the Spanish Football Federation postponed Wednesday’s Copa del Rey fixtures as a mark of respect. Everyone understands the gravity of what has happened, and Valverde’s response offers another example of why he commands so much respect as club captain. Leadership is often associated with performances, communication and responsibility on the pitch, but Valverde is also showing that it is important to know when football has to take a back seat. The Uruguayan is right to be doing what little he can to help in this situation, and Madrid should be proud to have someone like him as the team’s first captain.

item.title: Xabi Alonso says Chelsea 'played with courage' despite Carabao Cup shootout exit at Liverpool
item.description: Xabi Alonso says Chelsea 'played with courage' despite Carabao Cup shootout exit at Liverpool Xabi Alonso insists Chelsea 'played with courage' at Anfield, even as a 6-5 penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool ended their Carabao Cup run in the fourth round. The tie finished 1-1 after 90 minutes, with Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo both scoring from the spot in normal time. In the shootout, both sides missed penalties to win it, until the third round of sudden death, when Liverpool finally edged it. Liverpool will host Bournemouth in the quarter-finals. Chelsea also had to cope with an injury to Maxence Lacroix, while striker Emmanuel Emegha came off the bench for his debut only to see his penalty saved in the shootout. Wesley Fofana missed the decisive kick, blazing high over the bar, Defeat follows a disappointing loss to Tottenham in the Premier League at the weekend, but Alonso insisted he saw positives from his team. "For sure, the outcome is not what we wanted," Alonso said after the game. "It's not what we expected before the game. Once you reach penalties, there's going to be a sad side. "It is us in this case, but I have to say that during the game we have played at a very good competitive level, it was a good performance. We showed an improvement, I would say. That's what we wanted. "We played with courage. The game was really close, it could have gone either way. There were not many chances for both sides and we have tried to overcome difficult moments as well, like Max's [Lacroix] injury." The Chelsea boss had sympathy for Emegha. "It's hard to make your debut with that moment that could mean everything for him, for us," he said. "But it is about learning from all the experiences, even like today when it was a sad one. And I said it myself, as soon as we get on the bus, I move on, I think about United." Chelsea host Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday at 12.30pm, and Alonso was encouraged by how goalkeeper Mike Penders responded, after an error in the Tottenham loss. "He looked really solid with good composure, like he had dealt well with Saturday," he said. "That is what it takes in this job to overcome difficult situations and he did quite well. "It's a small setback but we need to move on. As soon as we leave Anfield, our focus is Saturday's Premier League game."

item.title: Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti admits Serie A table is weighing heavily on players' minds after shock Genoa defeat
item.description: Genoa CFC v Juventus FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Luciano Spalletti has expressed deep concern over the mental state of his Juventus squad following a damaging defeat against Genoa. The Bianconeri boss suggested that the club's current standing in the Serie A table is starting to negatively impact his players' performances on the pitch. Pressure mounting at Juventus Spalletti did not hide his frustration following Juventus' disappointing performance at Marassi, where they fell to a resilient Genoa side . The veteran coach pointed to the psychological burden currently affecting his squad, noting that the pressure of their league position is becoming a visible obstacle. With results failing to go their way, the weight of expectation appears to be hampering the team's ability to execute on matchdays. "It happens to me all too often now to be surprised by what I saw in the game played, which is different from what I saw in the previous one," the coach explained, as quoted by Sky Sport Italia . "The fact is that at Lecce I had seen certain things, then we didn't train and today I see other things. Nowadays we play at high rhythms, with great intensity, there are duels everywhere, and we continue to be fragile from this point of view; then they scored two goals also due to our responsibilities, we had a couple of chances ourselves and then everything became heavier. Even this league table we are living with and the results we have achieved are weighing a bit on our heads." Apologies to the Bianconeri faithful Understanding the gravity of the defeat and the poor quality of the performance, Spalletti used his post-match press conference to issue a direct apology to the travelling supporters. Fully aware of the gravity of the defeat and the lifeless nature of the performance, the tactician refused to hide behind excuses in his post-match press conference, making it his top priority to face the fans who made the journey before dissecting what went wrong on the pitch. "The first thing to do is to apologize to them, then we can talk about everything. If we have to talk about the difficulties we had tonight, it's quite easy. We were not at the level of physical impact and dueling. We lost everything from an intensity point of view," the manager stated. The Steelers celebrated their 16-10 victory with music, food, ice cream, and a memorable photo featuring Rodgers and veteran defensive lineman Cam Heyward. This Halloween season, check out the top five spookiest superstars to ever set foot in a WWE ring. 5. The Boogeyman Among WWE's roster of bionic rednecks and tribal chiefs lies The Boogeyman: a worm-eating demon who terrorized SmackDown from 2005 to 2007. Perhaps the most frightening-looking wrestler on this list, The Boogeyman grossed out audiences by devouring fistfuls of worms . Sometimes even his opponent would be forced to eat the worms after being defeated by the red-faced Boogeyman. His signature entrance featured The Boogeyman breaking a clock over his head as fog fills the arena. While not WWE's most technically gifted wrestler, The Boogeyman was a character firmly rooted in horror and horror comedy. The Boogeyman is simply absurd, but in a genuine way that only wrestling audiences could understand and love. The Boogeyman has made sporadic appearances in WWE for years, proving just how memorable and effective his horror imagery was. Fun fact: The Boogeyman is one of actor Timothée Chalamet's favorite wrestlers. 4. Gangrel and The Brood Gangrel and his associates Edge and Christian - known collectively as The Brood - were WWE's resident vampires during the company's vaulted Attitude Era of the late 1990s. The Brood looked like they stepped out of the nightclub in Blade and walked to the ring in what many consider to be one of the greatest theme songs of the era. The song, titled after their name, would work great in any haunted house. Gangrel, with his vampire teeth, would drink blood from a goblet before and after matches. Were the members of The Brood really vampires? Only time will tell; Edge and Christian, who went on to have hall of fame careers, still look pretty good for their age. 3. Kane (masked) The masked, secret brother of The Undertaker made a frightening entrance when he confronted The Deadman at Badd Blood: In Your House in 1997. Kane's famous first appearance featured The Big Red Machine ripping open the door to the Hell in a Cell cage in order to attack The Undertaker. Kane cost his brother the WWE Championship in a match against Shawn Michaels that was all but over. Kane's freaky red appearance, coupled with his tragic backstory of having survived a house fire that permanently damaged his face made him one of WWE's most recognizable faces of horror. What really made Kane scary, however, was how he was able to match The Undertaker in power and size. Suddenly The Undertaker didn't seem as powerful. item.description: “I feel she is…”: Eva Olid purrs over Man United hero Lea Schuller after 3-0 win vs. Burnley Manchester United head coach Eva Olid was full of praise for Lea Schuller following her outstanding performance in the 3-0 victory over Burnley in the Subway Players Cup. United win United came up against a stubborn Burnley side that played most of the game with a low block as they looked to frustrate their hosts. It took 29 minutes for United to breach the Burnley defence, with Ellen Wangerheim punishing an error from the goalkeeper. Schuller netted a brilliant double in the second half to secure the victory for United . It was an occasion with many positives for United. Beyond stretching their unbeaten run to nine games across all competitions, Olid welcomed back multiple players. Celin Bizet Donnum returned after more than a year out, having given birth in June. Jayde Riviere and Emma Watson also made their comebacks from injuries. Speaking to the media after the final whistle, Olid hailed Schuller while also encouraging her players to carry their momentum forward into the next game against Everton in the WSL. Olid’s remarks Olid said about Schuller, “She [Schuller] is growing in confidence this season and every time, I feel that she is better.” “There was help to grow in that confidence, we need her. It is good that everyone doing so well and the confidence is coming through and I am so happy for Ellen and the strikers too, so happy for both.” She said about the performance and result, “It was a little slow, the game, it is difficult to play against a low block, they went so deep and in a back five, it was so difficult to penetrate and difficult to find the spaces in the box.” “I think the first half the game was a little bit slow, the second half was a little more quicker and we could find the spaces from wide areas to the box and we could score the two goals that [made it] 3-0.” “It was a difficult game in terms of intensity but it is normal against a low block. At the end it is three goals, a clean sheet and we continue the good momentum.” On the players who returned, Olid remarked, “For me today, apart from the three goals and the points in the cup, that is the most important thing, the three coming back are so important and I know they are going to be so important for the team.” “We play a lot of matches, the squad is so competitive and I am so happy for them three.” Olid shared an update on Scarlet Hill, who was withdrawn in the second half with an apparent injury. “No update, I think it might be the calf but we need to check now.” The 41-year-old added, “This match is really good for momentum but we cannot relax on Saturday, we have Everton in the league. item.description: TOPSHOT - England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane reacts after receiving the Ballon d'Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d'Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images History was made on Monday night at the London Palladium. Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane was named the 2026 Ballon d’Or winner ahead of Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal. Kane became the first English player to win the award since Michael Owen all the way back in 20 01, and he also became the first Bayern player to win since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge did so in 1981, having als o won it in 1980. To add to the history, the England skipper was also the first Bundesliga player to be given the honor since Matthias Sammer back in 1996 when he played for Borussia Dortmund. For months, there was intense debate as to whether or not Kane would actually have a realistic shot at beating out the likes of Yamal and Mbappé to win, with France Football’s previous history of snubbing Bayern players casting justifiable doubt. Franck Ribéry had an incredibly strong case to win back in 2013, and likewise Robert Lewandowski in 2020 and 2021. Still, though, Kane was very much the deserved winner and was able to celebrate winning the Ballon d’Or on home soil on a night where he was also named striker of the year. It’s impossible to argue against the incredible year he had for club and country, having tallied an unprecedented 73 goals and 8 assists for Bayern and England, collecting a domestic double and England’s best World Cup finish (third) since 1966 along the way. France Football , L’Equipe , and the selected UEFA ambassadors and previous jury members that comprise the voting bodies for the Ballon d’Or have had their fair share of criticism throughout the years, especially in the wake of the era dominated by Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi. They’ve been labe led as populists in the past, but the amount of voting delegates who had Kane as their winner suggests that even what some consider to be a corrupt, sham election of sorts finally recognized a footballer who did all of his talking solely on the pitch, without any sort of media campaign or propaganda to help him get the award. As such, different voting tabs from various delegates from around the world have been making the rounds as we are now more than 24 hours removed from the ceremony in London. For the votes from Colombia (Pache Andrade) and Australia (Daniel Garb), both nations had Kane listed in first place, though Colombia had Rodri in second place and Australia had Mbap pé in second and Rodri in fourth (via @iMiaSanMia ). It goes to show that there were certainly differences amongst the top-five rankings from different voters, but Kane was unequivocally the deserved winner. item.title: ‘Stop being a victim’ – Fans have no sympathy for Pat McAfee even after he shares threatening DMs
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Pat McAfee is one of the most polarising figures in sports media, and even with him sharing the extent of the backlash he receives from fans, very few people feel bad for him. McAfee recently caused a stir after he expressed his dismay and anger over students at the University of Utah mocking him ahead of his visit with the College GameDay crew. McAfee even suggested that he was scared for his life, but many fans felt that he was blowing the situation extremely out of proportion. Pat McAfee shares DM threats, but fans don’t feel bad for him Taking to X , Pat McAfee put out a very lengthy post expressing his disappointment over the recent fan backlash that he has faced, with evidence of the kind of threats he has received. In a near 800-word post on X, McAfee expressed frustration over the recent criticism he has faced, suggesting that his only desire is to provide entertainment for sports fans. McAfee wrote: “I was created on the internet. I’ve been ‘cooked,’ s***talked and criticised since I have memories. I am nowhere near perfect, and there’s no way everybody is gonna agree with me, but I had no idea that this is just what life would become.” This very long post didn’t have the effect McAfee would have hoped for, as several fans pointed out that he was coming across as incredibly thin-skinned. One fan wrote: “Nobody from Utah said you were a corny creep.’ Stop embellishing for sympathy over a clear overreaction on your part.” Another fan added: “The two kids you are targeting are fantastic kids, who camped out to see you and made very lighthearted jokes. You should apologise to those kids… The situations are unrelated.” A third fan asked McAfee to get some perspective: “Dude, stop being a victim and a sensitive Karen. You make tens of millions of dollars to talk about sports on TV. Shut the actual f*** up and realise how lucky you are or get lost.” A fourth fan reminded the former Colts punter about his own role in the situation: “Let’s be real here. You took a joke by some Utah students and went Charmin soft and sensitive. Just remember – you signed up for this.” A fifth fan had some sound advice for the ESPN star: “Dude, you’ve got to step away for a year and let the fellas run your show. Take a step back from everything and get back to the roots. Get back to the mindset you had when starting the show in a basement in Indy. For your core fans. Too much going on right now.” And lastly, one final and longtime fan of McAfee’s pointed out just how much he has changed: “The fall off of McAfee has been wild to see. I remember when you went to ESPN, you said you didn’t sell out. Three years later, and your OG fans don’t even recognise you or the shill-slop character you’ve turned into.” Clearly, McAfee’s latest comments have not done much to alleviate any of the fan backlash he is facing, and many still believe he was in the wrong for what he said about the University of Utah. item.title: Liverpool forcing first-XI star out of the club, he wants to stay
item.description: Liverpool forcing first-XI star out of the club, he wants to stay Liverpool are forcing a first-XI player out of the club, per reports. This could be a massive mistake. Liverpool undoubtedly have big decisions to make with the future of first-team players. The squad build isn't complete - and arguably never is - but this is a particularly notable season for it. And good few senior players are out of contract, for one. The most notable being Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker. Liverpool would need pretty high-profile replacements for both, such is their influence in the team even after nearly nine years. But expiring contracts aren't all of it. There are also those will enter the final year of their deals - and that forces some major decisions at Anfield, too, as it represents a final chance to get decent money for a player. Alexis Mac Allister forced out of Liverpool? Sky Sports Switzerland report that Alexis Mac Allister could leave Liverpool in 2027. The club actually plan to get him gone, it seems, despite the fact he's been public about a desire to sign a new contract. Mac Allister's current deal runs until 2028. Next year will be the final time to get any money for him and it appears that Liverpool hope to sell the player and then use the funds to buy a replacement. Again, though, this isn't what Mac Allister wants. That's a real problem, too, as he's been a vital player for Liverpool this season and we'd put renewing his contract up there with Julian Ward's highest priorities . The Sky report suggests it won't happen. Liverpool committed major money to new contracts for both Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, making it clear that it's those players who they see forming their future in midfield. Mac Allister always looked quite left out - and reports like this one confirm that. Liverpool made their choice and even if the Argentine wishes his future was on Merseyside, he'll have little choice but to leave for a big contract elsewhere. He's in a difficult position, after all. Mac Allister will want to agree any contract with a club - including Liverpool - while he's still at the peak of his powers. Doing so after any sort of decline - or at any age closer to 30 - will reduce what he's offered. Liverpool will know he isn't willing to wait until 2028 to sort things and risk reduced offers. And that, ultimately, will force him out.

item.description: Zidane Iqbal (second left) helped Dundee United control the first half [Press Association] Do Dundee United have the best midfield three in the Scottish Premiership? With a man called Zidane at the heart of it all? That was the question being posed after Jim Goodwin's side stretched their unbeaten run to six games with a hard-earned 2-2 draw that prevented Celtic stretching their lead at the top of the table. United have slipped to fifth thanks to city rivals Dundee's 3-1 victory over Kilmarnock, and Irishman Goodwin was left disappointed his side had failed to win at Celtic Park for the first time in 52 games stretching back to 1992. But Goodwin, Celtic counterpart Martin O'Neill and the BBC pundits were full of praise for how they gave the reigning champions a fright and continue to impress. On BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound, chief sports writer Tom English asked "whether Dundee United have the best midfield three in Scotland right now". Former United wing-back Allan Preston enthused: "[Zac] Sapsford on the goal trail again and the guys in the middle of the park are great," he said. "Iqbal in that first half especially was pulling the strings and Celtic couldn't get near him. "Iqbal is like a watch battery. He keeps everything ticking. item.title: Iraola feels Liverpool togetherness growing after shootout win against Chelsea
item.description: Iraola feels Liverpool togetherness growing after shootout win against Chelsea Andoni Iraola has said he can feel the togetherness of his Liverpool side building after the Reds progressed to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals against Chelsea. Liverpool came out on top in a penalty shootout after a 1-1 draw at Anfield, after spot-kicks in normal time from Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo. Iraola's side won 6-5 on penalties, as Chelsea's Wesley Fofana missed the decisive kick. Both sides had already squandered earlier opportunities to win the shootout. Including shootout success, the win was Liverpool's fifth straight in all competitions. Iraola believes there is momentum building within his squad, ahead of a huge clash with Arsenal in the Premier League this weekend. "I feel it and I’m very happy to feel it because I think it’s very important. We need to feel what we are feeling now, the players are feeling. They are feeling the support of the ones in the stands and I think when we are all together, we create better atmospheres," he said at his post-match press conference. "Even starting losing, there was ‘Let’s go, come on.’ A lot of the players have given us very good help and now it’s the third game at home where we finish with good feelings. And we have another big one on Sunday and let’s try to finish this four in a row that we had at home in the best way." Iraola will face familiar opposition in the quarter-finals after Liverpool were drawn to face former club Bournemouth. The Spaniard admitted that the in-form Cherries were the side he most wanted to avoid. "Honestly, I was talking before the draw and I said, ‘The only team I don’t want is Bournemouth…’ For me, it’s special. They know me very well, they are playing very well lately, in a good moment. But it is what it is. We haven’t been very lucky with the draws – we have played Spurs and Chelsea already and now Bournemouth. That is going to be obviously special for me. But we have to earn the right to be in the semi-finals and I hope we can do it here at home again."

item.description: Pat Murphy Brewers Getty Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy praised the team’s fans after his squad won the 2026 World Series on Wednesday night. Murphy’s Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 of the World Series as they won the best-of-seven World Series by a final tally of 4-1. This is the first World Series championship in Brewers history, and Murphy is thrilled that he could help bring the Commissioner’s Trophy to the team’s incredible fans, who were there thick and thin for the team throughout what was the best season in franchise history. Pat Murphy Praises Brewers Fans Speaking to the media after Milwaukee won the 2026 World Series over the Rays, Murphy showered praise on the team’s fans. “We didn’t get picked to win the division by one outlet. We didn’t get picked to win over 85 games by anybody… but those fans of ours, they picked us,” Murphy said. #Brewers Pat Murphy on the championship parade this Friday and what it means to the fans, the city of Milwaukee and the state of Wisconsin: "We didn't get picked to win the division by one outlet. We didn't get picked to win over 85 games by anybody… but those fans of ours,… pic.twitter.com/Th7ZhG23wA — Lily Zhao (@LilySZhao) October 29, 2026 Pat Murphy Showers Brewers With Praise Just as much as Murphy has love for his team’s fans , the Brewers manager also has love for his team, and he spoke about them in glowing terms following Game 5. “This group of guys right here, the 2026 team, will be remembered forever — and they deserve that because they were a team. He is one, if not the best, managers in the game today, and he is someone whose players always play hard for him, even if he can be tough to play for sometimes, as he is known for benching players if they do not live up to the Brewers’ standards. item.description: Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe sets new La Liga benchmark with remarkable record Real Madrid have seen their attacking performances improve under Jose Mourinho in recent games, and one of the main reasons has been the form of Kylian Mbappe . The Frenchman’s explosive pace often helps him get into positions other attackers might struggle to reach and beat defenders in one-on-one situations. He remains the biggest threat in transition, and the latest statistics show just how quick he still is. Mbappe has registered the highest top speed of any player in La Liga this season, while also ranking among the fastest footballers across Europe’s five major leagues. Mbappe records fastest sprint in La Liga this season The 27-year-old has reached an impressive top speed of 36.3 km/h during the 2026-27 campaign, placing him ahead of every other player in the Spanish top flight. Across Europe’s five major leagues, only Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies has recorded a higher figure, reaching 36.7 km/h. Only Alphonso Davies has hit a higher top speed than Mbappe this season. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) Mbappe shares second place with several players, including Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, Inter Milan striker Marcus Thuram and Auxerre midfielder Naouirou Ahamada, who have also reached 36.3 km/h. Despite being almost 28, the Frenchman continues to be one of the fastest players in the world and has built his game around his pace. Mourinho finding ways to exploit Mbappe’s biggest strength The Frenchman has already scored 11 goals in ten La Liga appearances this season, including both goals in Madrid’s recent 2-1 Clasico victory over Barcelona. That said, what makes Mbappe very dangerous compared to other fast players is not simply his maximum running speed but his ability to recognise when to turn on the afterburners. Mourinho’s tactical set-up relies on Madrid settling into compact defensive structures and creating opportunities for quick transitions. Kylian is in excellent form so far this season. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images) Players like Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva have the vision and technical quality to release Mbappe into space at the perfect moment. As long as the Frenchman manages to stay onside, most defenders in the world cannot beat him in a foot race for a perfectly clipped ball. His movement remains Mbappe’s most valuable weapon, but the Frenchman will also know that he needs to expand his game beyond just that. There will come a time in his career, as he gets older, when his legs will not move as fast as they do at the moment. Elite players find ways to still influence games in such situations, and it remains to be seen how Mbappe’s game evolves as his career goes on.

item.title: WWE Just Dodged A Vince Russo-Shaped Bullet (WWE News)
item.description: VICE With reports coming out earlier this week that Vince Russo had held talks with WWE , and specifically WWE President Nick Khan, earlier this year, there's now an update on all of this. For those who missed it, Russo had several conversations with Khan this summer , complete with him either having visited WWE HQ or having been under consideration to visit WWE HQ. News of those conversations did not make it to wider WWE staff at the time, and influential names laughed off the idea of a return for the former WWE head writer when hearing of such talk. It was PWInsider who initially reported the Russo/Khan talks, and the outlet now adds that these conversations were initiated by Vince Russo. The former WCW World Heavyweight Champion reached out to Nick Khan to see about a potential role with WWE, though nothing came from those overtures. A WWE source confirmed to PWInsider that there was never a point in 2026 when the company was looking to hire Russo, with one other source joking that Vinny Ru will soon be "milking" this topic for his podcast, and jokingly suggesting he might end up signed to a WWE Legends deal alongside recent signee Necro Butcher . Vince Russo was previously with WWE from 1992 until late 1999, moving from freelance WWF Magazine writer to WWF Magazine editor, to the creative team, to the head of creative, and then jumping ship to WCW, where he'd remain until the company was purchased by Vince McMahon. An uber-brief WWE return would follow in 2002, before Russo instead moved to TNA, where he'd work on and off until 2014. Most recently, Russo had been involved as a writer, investor, and on-screen talent for Juggalo Championship Wrestling, though he announced his JCW departure last month. Which is Waqar Younis' favourite IPL team? Legendary Pakistani fast bowler and ex-captain Waqar Younis says that Sunrisers Hyderabad is one of his most loved Indian Premier League (IPL) sides. item.title: Barcelona loan watch: Ronald Araujo delivers yet another standout display in Chelsea win
item.description: Barcelona loan watch: Ronald Araujo delivers yet another standout display in Chelsea win Ronald Araujo delivered another commanding defensive performance for Liverpool against Chelsea in the League Cup, strengthening his case for a permanent stay in England while leaving Barcelona facing uncertainty over the defender’s long-term future. The Uruguayan has made an encouraging impression during his loan spell, having recently earned player of the match recognition following Liverpool’s league victory over Brighton. His latest display offered further evidence of his defensive value, with his contribution extending beyond the numbers on the scoresheet. Araujo dominates defensively in Liverpool victory over Chelsea Araujo was particularly effective at protecting Liverpool’s penalty area, reading danger early and clearing threatening deliveries before Chelsea could capitalise. He dealt confidently with balls into the box, including a cross from Jordan Henderson, while also helping Liverpool manage late pressure. Araujo was quite decisive against Chelsea. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) The defender even threatened at the other end. Timing his run like a centre-forward, Araujo launched himself at a header that looked capable of producing a goal, only for goalkeeper Mike Penders to deny him with an excellent save. His defensive statistics offered a striking illustration of his influence. Araujo recorded 10 clearances against Chelsea, while every other Liverpool defender combined managed just one. The figures alone explain how heavily Liverpool relied on him to deal with the visitors’ attacking threat. Liverpool hold €55 million option as Barcelona await decision Araujo’s performances have added weight to the possibility of a permanent transfer. Araujo’s loan as an option of permanent transfer. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) As reported before, Liverpool have an option to sign the defender for approximately €55 million, although the club have not yet made a final decision on whether to activate it. For Barcelona, that uncertainty leaves an important question over what happens when the loan arrangement reaches its conclusion. Araujo remains under contract with the Catalan club, so Liverpool’s intentions will play a major role in determining whether he stays in England or returns to Spain. A fee of that size would also represent a significant decision for Liverpool, while Barcelona must also consider their defensive plans and the player’s future role should he return.

item.title: How many games Danks could cover after Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital
item.description: How many games Danks could cover after Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital Vincent Kompany was discharged from the hospital on Wednesday evening. The Belgian head coach had been airlifted to the hospital last Friday after collapsing while watching FC Bayern’s second team in training. Following examinations, the club has released the following diagnosis: irritation of the meninges. Vincent Kompany has been released from the hospital (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) The former Burnley head coach will have no doubt been proud to see news of his Bayern side producing another consummate display in his absence with a 6-1 victory over FC Magdeburg in the DFB Pokal. A point of reassurance, really, is that while Kompany continues his recovery at his own pace, the club is in fine hands under assistant coach Aaron Danks. For now, the focus for the Belgian head coach has to be on recovering on his own timescale. How many games will Aaron Danks cover for Bayern? (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) Some commentators will no doubt be at pains to point out that victories over Magdeburg and SC Freiburg will be somewhat expected for a club of FC Bayern’s stature. However, we would quietly remind neutrals that Freiburg were one of the in-form sides in the Bundesliga before the Bavarians’ visit to the Europa-Park-Stadion at the weekend. That all said, an away trip to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League – sandwiched between Saturday’s Der Klassiker with Borussia Dortmund and the following weekend’s tie with Mainz – will be no picnic in the park. But the immediate priority has to be ensuring that Vincent Kompany has the time and space to recover – regardless of the pressing nature of key fixtures in the schedule. On that note, the 40-year-old is set to enjoy a break from the action until the next international break, as an absolute bare minimum . In that event, Kompany will miss the next handful of ties against Dortmund, Atletico and Mainz.

item.title: Wales make five changes as Lynn rewards bench
item.description: Bethan Lewis has captained Wales at the World Cup and in the Six Nations [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales have made five starting changes for Saturday's second WXV Test against Japan. Flanker Bethan Lewis will make her first start of the campaign, having been one of Wales' impressive impact players in last weekend's 17-0 victory in Tokyo, with co-captain Alex Callender moving to number eight. Gwen Crabb and Gwenllian Pyrs are also promoted from the bench to join the pack, while Lleucu George is preferred to Keira Bevan at fly-half. George will partner Seren Lockwood, who crossed for two tries last weekend, as Wales seek back-to-back wins (07:00 GMT). Courtney Keight comes in for centre Freya Bell, who looks set for a lengthy lay-off after suffering a serious knee injury in the opening Test. Head coach Sean Lynn has again opted for six forwards and two backs on the bench. "We have made the changes to reward the players who finished the job in Tokyo," said Lynn. Wales are looking to finish their WXV campaign on a high at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium, having previously beaten Japan and South Africa and narrowly lost to USA. They are ranked 11th in the world after overtaking Saturday's opponents with last week's victory. "The players know our DNA is 'team first'. Competition for places drives standards and performances and will only help us improve and get better as a team," Lynn added. "We are obviously disappointed with the injury to Freya Bell, but she will get the best care and we hope to see her back soon." While last weekend was another welcome win for Lynn, Wales made hard work of the victory in testing conditions. "We found a way in the first Test in Tokyo and the way the players problem-solved during the game was key for all the coaches," said Lynn. "But we know we have to be much more accurate and produce a consistent, 80-minute performance to beat a resilient Japan side that we know will be hurting." item.description: 7 duels won: Lewis Steele heaps praise on Liverpool hero who ‘rarely puts a foot wrong’ Lewis Steele saluted one Liverpool player who ‘rarely puts a foot wrong’ after the Reds’ penalty shootout triumph over Chelsea in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night. The tie was eventually settled in sudden death as Joe Gomez – who’s still yet to score for LFC in 280 appearances – buried his kick into the top corner of the net and Wesley Fofana then missed the target completely with his attempt. The 29-year-old elicited one of the biggest cheers of the night when he converted his penalty, capping a fine performance as he made the most of his recall to the starting XI at right-back. Steele heaps praise on Joe Gomez Taking to X just after the shootout ended, Steele applauded Liverpool’s longest-serving current player for his efforts on Wednesday, and indeed throughout his 11-and-a-bit seasons with the Reds so far. The Daily Mail reporter posted: ‘Putting aside the fact he morphed into a top striker for a second, what a night from Joe Gomez. No matter how many injuries he has or how little he plays, he very, very rarely puts a foot wrong.’ (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Gomez was terrific throughout the game against Chelsea, earning an 8/10 from Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle in his post-match player ratings as he enjoyed a compelling tussle with Blues attacker Morgan Rogers. The Reds’ number 2 could well revert to the substitutes’ bench for the weekend showdown against Arsenal, but last night he once again demonstrated his reliability to Liverpool and showed why he’s so adored by the Kop, giving everything for the cause even when his game-time is sporadic.

item.title: Regis Le Bris Must Continue Key Sunderland Change After Brentford Win
item.description: Sunderland beat Brentford 3-2 in improved attacking display from Le Bris' side Sunderland beat Brentford in the Carabao Cup fourth-round tie on Wednesday advance to book a spot in the quarter-finals at Crystal Palace, with Regis Le Bris' side enjoying one of, if not their best attacking display of the campaign thus far. As a result, the Sunderland boss must maintain the positive tactical changes that led to the Black Cats shell-shocking Keith Andrews' side with three goals in the space of 12 minutes in the first half, to help kickstart their Premier League campaign. Sunderland beat Brentford 3-2 courtesy of goals from young attacking trio Chemsdine Talbi, Timur Tutierov and Malick Fofana, who opened his Black Cats account after arriving from Lyon in the summer transfer window with a brave backpost header. Despite those three getting on the scoresheet and putting too much distance between the Black Cats and Brentford, it was young right-winger Jocelin Ta Bi who was the standout player for Sunderland , enjoying a hat-trick of assists for his teammates in a stunning breakout performance that oozed technical quality. With those four players, therein lies the tactical and selection change that Le Bris must maintain in the coming stages of the season, so that Sunderland can regain their attacking edge in the final third to get some Premier League wins back on the board. Sunderland celebrate Timur Tutierov's goal vs Brentford (IMAGO / Every Second Media) Regis Le Bris Must Continue Sunderland Calls After Brentford Win Against a strong Brentford side on Wednesdsay night, Sunderland scored more goals (three) in the opening 40 minutes against the Bees than they had done in their five outings combined before kick-off, netting against Torreense and Lech Poznan in the Europa League but firing blanks to Brighton, Bournemouth and Leeds United in the top flight. Clearly, when analysing the performance and selection decisions from Le Bris, Sunderland's improved attacking output was no coincidence. The Sunderland boss lined up with two natural wingers in Fofana and Ta Bi, with Talbi operating in a central role behind young forward Tutierov, seeing the athletic central midfield duo of Jules Ahoka and Habib Diarra also offer options and runs from deep to support. With Le Bris resisting the urge to use a right-back at the right-wing position, Sunderland looked far more potent, creative and dynamic in attack, which has been a glaring issue for the Black Cats at the start of the campaign, particularly in the Premier League, with Sunderland bottom of the table for goals per match (0.8). Crucially, however, the possession stats from the Carabao Cup win over Brentford also tell an interesting story, with Sunderland having just 33 percent possession in the first half on Wednesday night, but scoring three goals in the process.
